A very loose, grainy wet-on-wet watercolor painting on rough cold-press paper, ultra-wide 21:9, of the following scene.
Reference images: the first is the approved village-at-dawn cut and sets the painting style above all (soft blooms, granulating pigment, white paper left for light); the second, third and fourth are further style paintings of the same kind. Take only technique, brushwork and paper texture from these four, never their subjects, colors or composition. The fifth is the approved colour cut: take only its colors, light and mood, never its landscape and never its direction of light.
Scene: a river village seen from a low hill, camera angle about 30 degrees down; the river crosses the lower third from left to right; clustered tile-roofed houses fill the right of the middle third; the upper third is pale sky with distant ridges. Two small figures, far apart, on the riverbank path.
Light: early morning, sun low from the left, long soft shadows toward the right, colour range from pale peach to cool blue-grey.
Style: large smooth washes for walls and water, tiny dabs for leaves and sky; soft lost edges, no outlines.
Look of the place: period-accurate wooden boats and tile roofs; the same houses and village layout as the other cuts.
Composition: the main houses stay inside the visible band between 23% and 77% from the top; the lower centre holds only riverbank grass.
Not a photograph, 3D render, game art or detailed digital illustration; no pen outlines, vignette, text, border, power lines or modern cars.
